name: Protection / Lightsmith
note: CANONICAL, hand-edited. Generates CombatAssistPlus/Catalogs/Protection.lua via `wowkb.capart export catalog protection`, and the per-ability state table the preview draws. The Lightsmith roster; Templar is a separate catalog authored later, not a second overlay bolted on here. ⚠ `hero` is deliberately unset: the Paladin hero sub-tree ids have not been read from a live client, and inventing one would silently bind nothing. Unset means "any hero tree" — and unlike Retribution, whose roster was spec-wide, THIS roster is Lightsmith-specific, so a Templar Protection Paladin gets a catalog built around an armament row their build does not have. That is real exposure, not a formality. ⚠ NO `power` field, measured rather than omitted: the 12.1 Protection priority list carries no `holy_power` term of any kind. "Paladin ⇒ declare HolyPower" is exactly the inference the second Paladin catalog invites, and it is wrong. ⚠ NO row declares `charged`, and four of them would want to — this repo carries no Tier-1 charge count for Holy Armaments, Shield of the Righteous or Crusader Strike, and Judgment's second charge is talent-conditional. The consequence is that `capped` has no subject anywhere in this catalog. Base spell ids only: Bind unions base/override/tooltip/live into the row, so neither the Sacred Weapon nor the Hammer of Wrath transform needs a hardcoded override id.
talents_note: Node + entry from `knowledge/classes/paladin/protection/ability-inventory.tsv` @ 12.1. ⚠ `divine_guidance` and `blessed_assurance` SHARE node 95235, and that is the fact rather than a typo: they are the Lightsmith choice node at 8,11, so exactly one of them exists on any build and the other is dead. Two markers are gated on it in opposite directions. ⚠ The key `divine_guidance` appears in BOTH families and that is legal — `Catalog.Check` keys `abilities` and `talents` in separate tables and the `talent` predicate resolves only the second. The aura is the stacking buff; the talent is whether the buff can exist at all.

entries.note: Rung 5. A PLACED cooldown: its value is set by what lands inside it, and Divine Toll's clock is the whole of that. Sealed, so the hold is a band.

states.exception: On cooldown. No rung expresses it — a priority list only ever says when to press, and Blizzard's swipe rules the row out before cap has an opinion of its own.

states.condition: ready, Divine Toll within 10s or already ready
states.note: Rung 5 fires at `cooldown.divine_toll.remains<=10`, so this is the press window.

⚠ The sense is `beyond`, and getting it backwards would invert the button. The rung FIRES at `remains<=10`, so the HOLD is the complement: Divine Toll is nowhere near, so this is not its moment. The band also reads nothing at zero remaining, which is correct here — a READY Divine Toll satisfies `remains<=10` and must not hold anything. ⚠ NO SCENARIO REACHES THIS STATE; it is declared from the marker, not observed in a walk.

entries.note: Rung 7, the spec's largest Holy Power injection, and it belongs inside Wings. ⚠ The rung has two disjuncts and only the second is authorable: the first is `buff.avenging_wrath.up`, and whether a Category-3 (TrackedBar) row raises the `aura` latch's alert edges is UNMEASURED. A latch on an unmeasured edge is a hold that may never release, so it is not authored.

states.exception: On cooldown. No rung expresses it — a priority list only ever says when to press, and Blizzard's swipe rules the row out before cap has an opinion of its own.

states.condition: ready, Wings near or Righteous Protector talented
states.note: ⚠ Righteous Protector is near-mandatory and DELETES this cue: it halves Avenging Wrath's cooldown, which removes the disjunct from the priority. So on the build almost everyone plays, Divine Toll wears nothing and this is the only ready state. Stated as a hole rather than papered over with an approximation.

states.condition: ready, Righteous Protector UNtalented, Avenging Wrath within 30s
states.note: `within = 30` is the complement of `remains>30` and is correct across the entire 120s cooldown without Righteous Protector.

entries.note: Rung 9, the spender and the active mitigation. ⚠ Rung 9 is UNCONDITIONAL on Lightsmith by derivation rather than by reading: every term in its condition is Templar's, so with no Hammer of Light on the build the first disjunct is trivially true. The row needs no press gate at all, which is why the spender's placement is pure position — and why its one marker is about affordability instead.

states.exception: On cooldown. No rung expresses it — a priority list only ever says when to press, and Blizzard's swipe rules the row out before cap has an opinion of its own.
Affordability is not a rung. The priority list assumes the resource is there — simc simply skips an action it cannot pay for — so this is cap re-presenting a cost, not a line of its own.
states.note: ⚠ R1's warning applies exactly: a spender whose cost is the only thing between it and a press raises no readiness edge for that cost, so Blizzard's border cannot say this. It is shown castable, it is off the global, and it is the button pressed out of habit at the wrong Holy Power. The client also tints it `not-enough-power` — that tint is Blizzard's and cap neither draws nor undoes it.

states.exception: On cooldown. No rung expresses it — a priority list only ever says when to press, and Blizzard's swipe rules the row out before cap has an opinion of its own.

states.condition: ready, in its HOLY BULWARK life, Avenging Wrath beyond 5s
states.note: One button, two jobs, and which job it has right now is written only on the icon's own artwork. As Holy Bulwark it wants SAVING until Wings. ⚠ The hold is wrong at two charges (rung 23) and no `charged` is declarable on this spec, so it keeps drawing where the priority would dump the charge — a named defeat, not a footnote.

states.condition: ready, in its SACRED WEAPON life
states.note: ⚠ Quiet by DESIGN and that is the named exposure. The identity gate is load-bearing in both directions: without it the hold would sit on this life, where the correct press is now; with it, this life carries no cue at all, because rung 10's `buff.sacred_weapon.remains<6` is an aura-remaining band nobody has written.

states.condition: ready, Holy Bulwark life, Avenging Wrath within 5s
states.note: The hold releases: this is the window the bulwark was being banked for.

entries.note: Rungs 13 and 18. It FEELS like the top of the rotation and rung 18 is the low unconditional one, with three rungs between it and rung 13. Only Glory of the Vanguard genuinely puts it first — which is why the Vanguard term is a READABLE GATE on a sealed display, the `when`-beside-`display` shape. Without it the hatch would rule out the row in the one state rung 13 puts it first.

states.exception: On cooldown. No rung expresses it — a priority list only ever says when to press, and Blizzard's swipe rules the row out before cap has an opinion of its own.

states.note: Rung 18, the low unconditional one, which is the ordinary press for most of a fight.

states.condition: ready, Judgment TRANSFORMED to Hammer of Wrath and ready, Vanguard absent
states.note: Rung 16 puts Hammer of Wrath above this row. Cue E.

states.condition: ready, Vanguard absent, Divine Guidance talented, its count at five or more
states.note: ⚠ The first sealed display in ANY catalog that rules out a row the aura does not belong to. Demonology's two count tables both sat on the row whose own press the count gated; here the count is Divine Guidance's, the entry is Avenger's Shield, and the statement is "the row to your right outranks this one right now". The mechanism needs nothing new — `Channel.Plan` binds `display.ability` independently of `entry.ability` — but the STATEMENT is a relationship rather than a self-test. ⚠ The direction is V16 and not V17, and that choice is the whole of whether it is honest: drawn the other way it would say "ruled out until Divine Guidance is capped", which is false.

states.condition: ready, Hammer of Wrath armed AND the Divine Guidance band drawing
states.note: Both markers true at once. ⚠ The co-occurrence gate does not demand this pair be stated — it only pairs markers that carry a CUE, and `as_guidance_capped` carries none — so it is written down here on purpose rather than because something asked for it.

entries.note: Rungs 15, 19, 24 and 29. ⚠ Rungs 19 and 24 are not modelled: `!consecration.up` reads a Category-3 (TrackedBar) row, the same unmeasured alert-edge question as Avenging Wrath's buff.

states.exception: On cooldown. No rung expresses it — a priority list only ever says when to press, and Blizzard's swipe rules the row out before cap has an opinion of its own.

states.note: The most-pressed button in the rotation and the one with the least visible reason — rungs 15, 19, 24 and 29 behind one identical icon.

states.condition: ready, Judgment transformed to Hammer of Wrath and ready, Divine Guidance talented, its count below five
states.note: ⚠ The complement's readable gate is what makes it TRUE, and this is the answer to Demonology's warning rather than an exception to it. Below five stacks Consecration is not eliminated in general — rung 19 presses it whenever the ground effect is down. The gate narrows the display to the one state where the low band IS an elimination: while Hammer of Wrath is armed and off cooldown, where rung 16 outranks rung 19. Outside that gate the client is never asked to paint anything. ⚠ With no Divine Guidance aura at all the table has no subject and NOTHING covers that state; the readable marker that filled it was deleted for DENSITY, not for being wrong.

entries.note: Rungs 17, 22 / 16. ⚠ Rung 17 is not authored — the second-charge dump, and `charged` is undeclarable on this spec.

states.exception: On cooldown. No rung expresses it — a priority list only ever says when to press, and Blizzard's swipe rules the row out before cap has an opinion of its own.

states.condition: ready, or in its HAMMER OF WRATH life
states.note: In its Hammer of Wrath life it needs nothing: it outranks the two rows to its left, and both of those wear cue E to say so.

states.condition: ready, BASE life, Blessed Assurance talented and its aura up
states.note: Blessed Assurance makes the hammer to its right worth more for exactly one cast. ⚠ The identity term is not decoration: rung 16 puts Hammer of Wrath above both hammer rungs, so the yield must VANISH while the row is transformed — otherwise the row that just earned cue E on two neighbours would stand itself down.

entries.note: Rungs 20, 21 / 25, 26. ⚠ Its Blessed Assurance promotion is expressed on Judgment (cue F), not here: this row does not change KIND under the buff, and a rank change within one kind is what the left-to-right scan already carries.

states.exception: On cooldown. No rung expresses it — a priority list only ever says when to press, and Blizzard's swipe rules the row out before cap has an opinion of its own.

states.note: The filler, reached by subtraction. No cue solves anything here. ⚠ The row declares NO band on `identity` even though it is a choice node: both hammers have zero CooldownSetSpell rows, so exactly one exists on a build and reaches the Cooldown Manager permanently on 35395 — the transform is always on, and a band would encode a distinction that never varies.

entries.note: Rung 28. A Holy Power heal competing with the active mitigation for the same three Holy Power.

states.note: The priority presses this in exactly one state: free. Without the proc the button has no place in the damage priority at all, so the hold is load-bearing the way Demonology's `db_awaits_core` is — it holds the row in EVERY other state, which is also why no `starved` marker is authored here: a second badge would say the same thing twice.
No cooldown state: Word of Glory has no cooldown of its own.

entries_note: Entry order IS the authored priority, and it is the flattened `actions.default` — one list, no sub-lists and no hero fork, with four rows whose rungs straddle another row's. `Catalog.OrderCheck` reports when the player's Cooldown Manager disagrees with it.
